UNRESOLVED. These two are algebraically the same quantity -- as t -> inf the modal
sum tends to 2 G_ii, and <R^2_ij> tends to G_ii + G_jj - 2 G_ij -> 2 G_ii once
G_ij decays. They differ by a factor of 3.00, and I have NOT
identified why. Two candidates are visible and neither was confirmed: the MSD is
averaged over 24 loop configurations while <R^2> is read off one, and G_ij
may not have decayed at the separation sampled. It is recorded as an open defect
rather than argued away, because a model whose own two formulas disagree by 3x has
something wrong in it whatever the downstream numbers look like.

THE MODEL HAS A TIME AXIS AND IT IS CHEAP. Two clocks: relaxation inside a fixed loop set,
in closed form from the modes, and rewiring of the loop set itself from the KMC. The whole
dynamics cost 49s on four CPUs, because no trajectory is ever integrated.
AND IT REPRODUCES THE THING SINGLE-CELL HI-C FOUND: no individual configuration looks
like the map. TADs here are a property of the population, exactly as extrusion predicts.
